columns.label: Socioeconomic classification, 2013 version
columns.note: This is the version to use. It runs from 1991, so it reaches back further than its name suggests and covers the periods of the three older versions as well.

columns.name: socio02
columns.label: Socioeconomic classification, 2002 version
columns.note: Uses socio13's lookup, but the two do not fully agree. Checked 2026-09-09 against DST's own value tables (https://www.dst.dk/da/TilSalg/ data-til-forskning/generelt-om-data/dokumentation-af-data/hoejkvalitetsvariable/ Personers-tilknytning-til-arbejdsmarkedet-set-over-hele-aaret--AKM-/SOCIO02): code 111 here is "10 or more employees", the same boundary socio13 uses, so socio02 and socio13 read together safely. `socio` (the 1994-2001 predecessor) is the one that disagrees: see its own reader_note.

columns.name: socio
columns.label: Socioeconomic classification, 1994-2001 version
columns.note: Uses socio13's lookup, but the two do not agree on code 111. Checked 2026-09-09 against DST's own value tables (https://www.dst.dk/da/TilSalg/ data-til-forskning/generelt-om-data/dokumentation-af-data/hoejkvalitetsvariable/ Personers-tilknytning-til-arbejdsmarkedet-set-over-hele-aaret--AKM-/SOCIO): here, 111 is "selvstaendig med 50 eller flere ansatte" (self-employed, 50+ employees). In socio02 and socio13, the same code 111 is "10 eller flere ansatte" (10+ employees). The size boundary moved and the code did not change, so a self-employed person with, say, 20 employees is 111 in one era and a different code in the other, with nothing in the data to flag the switch.

columns.name: famaekvivadisp_13
columns.label: Household-equivalised disposable income
columns.note: This is the family's disposable income divided by an equivalence factor, so that families of different sizes can be compared. The factor counts the first adult as 1.0, each further person over 14 as 0.5, and each child under 15 as 0.3: a couple with two young children comes to 1 + 0.5 + 0.6 = 2.1, so a family income of 420,000 is recorded as 200,000 for each of the four. `FAMDISPONIBEL_13` is the same money before that division, and `FAMAEKVIVAINDKNETTO` is a different income concept (total income with net interest), so check which one your analysis plan means. The `_13` suffix marks the definition that replaced the older variables from 2013: DST states that FAMDISPONIBEL was discontinued in 2013 and replaced by FAMDISPONIBEL_13. A study spanning 2013 has to know which side of that change it is on. DST's year ranges settle the relationship with the sister column FAMAEKVIVADISP, which has no _13: the old one runs 1990-2012, this one runs 1987-2024. The _13 definition was applied backwards as well as forwards, so it is not a newer variable covering later years only. A study spanning the 2013 changeover should use _13 for the whole period rather than splicing the two, which would mix two definitions in one series.
columns.derivation: FAMAEKVIVADISP_13 = FAMDISPONIBEL_13 / (1 + (0.5 * (number of people over 14 in the family - 1)) + (0.3 * number of people under 15 in the family))

columns.name: year
columns.label: Register year
columns.note: Not a DST variable. It comes from fastreg's parquet conversion, which concatenates the yearly deliveries, so it exists in the data you read but not in DST's own documentation of this register.
columns.origin: not a DST variable - added by fastreg

columns.name: famaekvivadisp
columns.label: Equivalised disposable family income
columns.note: The same weighting scheme as FAMAEKVIVADISP_13 below, just algebraically rearranged on the source page: the first adult over 14 counts as 1.0, each further person over 14 as 0.5, and each child under 15 as 0.3. All persons belonging to the same family on 31 December of the income year (same E-familienummer), including resident children under 25, are assigned the family's equivalised income. `FAMDISPONIBEL` is the same money before that division.
columns.derivation: FAMAEKVIVADISP = FAMDISPONIBEL / (0.5 + (0.5 * number of people over 14 in the family) + (0.3 * number of people under 15 in the family))

columns.name: famaekvivaindknetto
columns.label: Equivalised total income including net interest
columns.derivation: FAMAEKVIVAINDKNETTO = FAMSUMINDKNETTORENT / (0.5 + (0.5 * number of people over 14 in the family) + (0.3 * number of people under 15 in the family))

columns.label: Personal identifier
columns.note: Results carrying only a replacement CPR number are filtered out before the research table is built, so every row here has a real personal identifier. The narrower `laboratorieproevesvar` table calls this column `cprnummer`.
columns.type_source: Dokumentation af Laboratoriedatabasens Forskertabel v4: Format CHAR, Laengde 10

columns.name: samplingdate
columns.label: Sampling date
columns.note: When the sample was taken, not when the result was reported. This guide previously called the column `samplingdato`, which does not exist.

columns.name: samplingtime
columns.label: Sampling time
columns.note: Not in the narrower `lab_forsker` table.

columns.name: analysiscode
columns.label: Analyte code
columns.note: Which analysis was done, coded in NPU or the Danish DNK terminology. This is the column the guide used to call `npu`, which does not exist. Only NPU- and DNK-coded results reach the research table, about 95 per cent of all results: anything coded with a laboratory's own local code is absent.

columns.name: value
columns.label: Result
columns.note: Text, not a number. Alongside numeric results the table holds a fixed set of words: POSITIV, NEGATIV, NORMAL, IKKE PAAVIST, PAAVIST, INGEN VAEKST, FORHOEJET and the blood-type codes. as.numeric() turns every one of those into NA without warning, which drops exactly the samples where something was found. The narrower `laboratorieproevesvar` table calls this column `samplevalue`.

columns.name: unit
columns.label: Unit
columns.note: Never compare values across laboratories without checking this. Different equipment and sample material mean the same analyte code can need different interpretation, within one laboratory over time as well.

columns.name: resulttype
columns.label: Result type
columns.note: Whether the result is numeric or alphanumeric. Use it to split the two before converting anything.

columns.name: laboratorium_idcode
columns.label: Laboratory identifier
columns.note: A MedCom laboratory code. Coverage starts at different dates per laboratory, so this column is what tells you whether a gap in a series is clinical or administrative.

columns.name: resultvalidation
columns.label: Result validation
columns.note: Not in the narrower `lab_forsker` table.

columns.name: operator
columns.label: Operator
columns.note: Carries the "less than" or "greater than" sign when a result is reported as below or above a detection limit. Ignoring it turns a censored value into an exact one.

columns.name: pnr
columns.label: Personal identifier
columns.note: DST's variable list calls this column `PNR12`. Check whether your variable is named `pnr` or `pnr12`. Do not confuse this with the `pnr` documented on esundhed's page for this register (DocumentationExtended?id=14): that `pnr` is the pharmacy or manufacturer's production-unit number, length 10, not a person. Same name, unrelated variable, on the two pages that between them cover this register.

columns.name: DW_EK_BORGER

columns.name: DW_EK_FORLOEB_FORRIGE

columns.name: DW_EK_HELBREDSFORLOEB

columns.name: FORL_AFSLUT_MAADE

columns.name: FORL_HENV_TIDSPUNKT
columns.label: Referral time

columns.name: FORL_HENV_MAADE
columns.label: Referral method code

columns.name: FORL_HENV_AARSAG
columns.label: Referral reason (diagnosis) code

columns.name: FORL_HENV_INSTANS
columns.label: Referring authority code

columns.note: Free-hospital-choice (frit sygehusvalg) indicator, by the variable name. columns.name: FORL_ANS

columns.name: FORL_INST_EJERTYPE
columns.label: Responsible institution owner type

columns.name: FORL_ANS_GEO_REG

columns.note: No unique key exists for this table (Sundhedsdatastyrelsen's LPR3_F guidance, section 3.9): every row hangs off the course it was registered on.

columns.name: DW_EK_HELBREDSFORLOEB
columns.label: Health course identifier
columns.note: A level above dw_ek_forloeb, not documented anywhere else in this schema - a helbredsforloeb can group several forloeb rows. Not confirmed to match any single row in lpr_a_forloeb.yaml one-to-one.

columns.name: LPRINDBERETNINGSSYSTEM
columns.label: Reporting system
columns.note: Filter to 'LPR3' when combining with LPR2, or the same marker risks being counted under both systems.

columns.name: MARKOER
columns.label: Marker code
columns.note: Three logical kinds share this one column, distinguished only by which code fires: a single-event marker (e.g. informed consent given), a period-start marker (e.g. referred for workup), or a period-end marker (e.g. cancer pathway ended). columns.name: MARKOER_INDB_TIDSPUNKT
columns.label: Marker reporting time
columns.note: When the marker was reported to LPR3, not necessarily when the event happened - see markoer_tidspunkt for that.

columns.name: MARKOER_TEKST
columns.label: Marker, text
columns.note: The text label for markoer - the practical way to read this column without a SKS browser lookup.

columns.name: MARKOER_TIDSPUNKT
columns.label: Marker event time
columns.note: By LPR3_F's own definition (section 3.9) a marker IS its timestamp - this is the actual event time, distinct from markoer_indb_tidspunkt (when it was reported).

columns.name: DW_EK_KONTAKT
columns.label: Contact identifier
columns.note: A referral reason can be registered on a course OR a contact (Sundhedsdatastyrelsen's LPR3_F guidance, section 3.10): a row here may have one of dw_ek_forloeb/dw_ek_kontakt populated and the other empty, not necessarily both.

columns.name: dw_ek_kontakt
columns.label: Contact identifier
columns.note: The key the diagnosis and procedure tables join on.

columns.name: dw_ek_forloeb
columns.label: Course identifier

columns.name: kont_starttidspunkt
columns.label: Contact start
columns.note: A datetime, not a date. as.Date() it before comparing with an index date.

columns.name: lprindberetningssystem
columns.label: Reporting system
columns.note: Filter to "LPR3". The table reaches back to 2017, and the outpatient contacts from before March 2019 are also in LPR2, so combining the two without this filter counts the same contact twice. This is a different thing from LPR_F vs LPR_A: those are two file formats, a choice made before you even open a file, not a value this column can hold. See the lprindberetningssystem code system for the full value set and its confidence levels.

columns.name: dw_sk_sygehusophold
columns.label: Hospital stay identifier
columns.note: A stay can gather several contacts. Counting rows here is not the same as counting admissions.

columns.name: dw_ek_borger
columns.label: Citizen identifier
columns.note: An internal person key. Use pnr for joins to other registers; this one does not travel outside LPR3.

columns.name: adiag
columns.label: Primary diagnosis
columns.note: The contact's action diagnosis, repeated here so simple analyses need not join lpr_a_diagnose. Secondary diagnoses are only in the diagnosis table, so filtering on this column alone misses them.

columns.name: prioritet
columns.label: Priority
columns.note: The code ATA1 marks an acute contact. Together with the contact's duration this is how LPR3 substitutes for LPR2's c_pattype.

columns.name: kont_indb_tidspunkt
columns.label: Reporting time
columns.note: When the contact was reported, not when it happened. Recent months look incomplete because reporting lags.

columns.name: flag_kont_afsluttet
columns.label: Contact closed flag
columns.note: An open contact has no end time yet, so durations computed near the end of the data are wrong rather than missing.

columns.name: kont_ans_geo_reg
columns.label: Region of the treating unit, geographic

columns.name: kont_ans_geo_reg_tekst
columns.label: Region of the treating unit, text

columns.name: kont_ans_org_reg
columns.label: Region of the treating unit, organisational

columns.name: borger_koen
columns.label: Sex
columns.note: Sex as recorded on the contact, as text rather than a number. **No published source gives its value set, so this schema records none.** Checked without success: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen's Vejledning til LPR3_F, which documents these very research tables; the LPR3 reporting guidance; esundhed's LPR documentation, which covers LPR2 only; and DST's variable list, which names the column but gives neither label nor values. Treat this as settled rather than as something still to look up. The neighbouring register is no guide either: LPR2's c_sex switched from 1/2 to M/K in 2005, so both codings exist in the family and neither can be assumed here. If you need sex as a study variable, take koen from BEF, which is documented and stable; if you need what the hospital recorded, check what your own column contains before filtering on it.

columns.name: borger_foedselsdato
columns.label: Date of birth

columns.name: borger_doedsdato
columns.label: Date of death
columns.note: A death date carried on the contact. It is not a death register: use DOD for mortality, or you only see people who had a hospital contact.

columns.label: Age in years at contact end

columns.name: DW_EK_BORGER_BARN
columns.label: Child's citizen identifier
columns.note: A citizen data-warehouse key for the child, alongside the plain PNR_BARN - LPR3's own internal identifier, not something to join other registers on directly.

columns.name: BORGER_KOEN_BARN
columns.label: Child's sex code
columns.note: The child's sex. Not confirmed to share `koen`'s numeric or `mfr_koen`'s letter encoding - DST gives no value definition here.

columns.name: DW_EK_FORLOEB_BARN

columns.label: Child's course label code

columns.name: FORL_LABEL_BARN_TEKST
columns.label: Child's course label, text
columns.note: The text label for FORL_LABEL_BARN - this _TEKST-suffix pattern (a code column plus its own derived-text sibling) recurs across most other columns in this register and the rest of the LPR_A_* family newly found in this same pass.

columns.name: FORL_REF_TYPE_BARN
columns.label: Child's course reference type code
columns.note: How the child's course element is referenced, the same concept as mfr_barn_forloeb.yaml's own ForloebReferenceMaade.

columns.name: CPRTJEK
columns.label: CPR check code
columns.note: Same name as ftbarn.yaml's own CPRTJEK - not confirmed to share its meaning or values, DST documents neither.

columns.name: dw_ek_kontakt
columns.label: Contact identifier
columns.note: The key to lpr_a_kontakt, which is where pnr lives. This table carries no person identifier of its own.

columns.name: proc_starttidspunkt

columns.name: proc_kode_type
columns.label: Procedure code type
columns.note: "P" marks a procedure, "+" an add-on code. An add-on code modifies the procedure above it and is not a procedure in its own right, so counting all rows overcounts.

columns.label: Parent procedure code
columns.note: LPR3 nests procedures the same way it nests diagnoses: an add-on code points at the procedure it belongs to.

columns.name: dw_ek_forloeb
columns.label: Course identifier
columns.note: One level above the contact. Where dw_ek_kontakt is empty, this is the only route back to a person, and it reaches a whole course of treatment rather than a single contact.

columns.name: flag_proc_uden_kont
columns.label: Procedure without a contact
columns.note: Flags a procedure with no contact attached. Those rows cannot be joined to lpr_a_kontakt at all, so a plain inner join drops them silently.

columns.name: lprindberetningssystem
columns.label: Reporting system
columns.note: Filter to "LPR3" when combining with LPR2, or contacts reported under both systems are counted twice.

columns.name: proc_indb_tidspunkt
columns.label: Reporting time

columns.name: DW_SK_SYGEHUSOPHOLD

columns.name: FLAG_PROC_UDEN_KONT
columns.label: Procedure without a contact

columns.name: PROC_KODE_TYPE
columns.label: Procedure code type

columns.name: PROC_PARENT_KODE

columns.name: PROC_SLUTTIDSPUNKT
columns.label: Procedure end
columns.note: For a cancelled registration, likely the planned rather than actual end - not confirmed by any documentation found.

columns.name: PROC_STARTTIDSPUNKT
columns.label: Procedure start
columns.note: Likely the planned rather than actual start, for the same reason as proc_sluttidspunkt - not confirmed.

columns.name: DW_EK_FORLOEB
columns.label: Course identifier
columns.note: A result report is always tied to at least a course, per LPR3_F's guidance (section 3.7) - dw_ek_forloeb should be the most reliably populated of the three join keys here.

columns.name: RES_INDB_ANS
columns.label: Result reported by code

columns.name: RES_TYPE

columns.name: afrper

columns.name: sikgrup
columns.label: Insurance group
columns.note: Group 1 patients need a referral from their GP to see a specialist, physiotherapist, chiropodist or psychologist, and pay nothing. Group 2 patients may go directly to any GP or specialist, but pay the difference between the fee and the regional subsidy themselves. The two groups therefore leave different traces for the same clinical need, so group membership is a confounder in any analysis of specialist use. Source: borger.dk, "Sygesikring og sikringsgrupper".

atc.name: ATC (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical)
atc.description: The WHO classification of medicines. Five cumulative levels: 1 character (anatomical main group), 3 (therapeutic subgroup), 4 (pharmacological subgroup), 5 (chemical subgroup), 7 (chemical substance). Each level repeats the levels above it and adds characters, so C09AA05 contains C, C09, C09A and C09AA.
atc.note: As a rule, filter on the full 7-character code rather than on the level columns: `atc2` holds three characters, so a longer pattern matched against it can never match, and it returns nothing at all with no error. The level columns are well suited to grouping, and to filtering when every code you want is the same length as the column.

beskst.name: Beskaeftigelsesstatus, 1976-2001 (AKM/Indkomst)
beskst.description: A person's main labour-market position during the year: self-employed, an employee, a pensioner, or one of a few other categories. The predecessor to beskst02, with a shorter, coarser code list.
beskst.note: Not comparable with beskst02, in DST's own words, not just a difference of degree: people with an unemployment share over 50 percent, and people on efterløn (early retirement pay), get their own codes under beskst02 that this code list does not have, and the rules for who counts as self-employed also changed. See beskst02's reader_note.

beskst02.name: Beskaeftigelsesstatus, 2002 onwards (AKM/Indkomst)
beskst02.description: A person's main labour-market position during the year. Longer and finer than the 1976-2001 predecessor (beskst): it splits out efterløn, dagpenge and kontanthjælp recipients as their own categories instead of folding them into broader ones. Shared by beskst02 and beskst13, which use the same codes.
beskst02.note: Not comparable with beskst (see beskst's own reader_note): DST states this directly, not just a difference of degree. Comparable with beskst13 with named exceptions: self-employment income is measured net of capital income in beskst13 rather than gross, and beskst13's amount thresholds are price-adjusted where beskst02's are not. A study spanning both should read DST's own change note before treating them as one continuous series.

c_dodsmaade.name: Doedsmaade, to 2001 (DAR t_dodsaarsag_1)
c_dodsmaade.description: How the person died, as coded in the FIRST cause-of-death table, which is what dodsaars holds. The set was reorganised on 1 January 1991, and the lookup below is the one in force from that date. A second, different set of numbers is used from 2002: see `c_dodsmaade_2002`.
c_dodsmaade.note: Two separate traps. First, this code set is NOT the one used from 2002: in dodsaasg the same column holds `c_dodsmaade_2002`, where 1 is Voldshandling rather than Naturlig død. Second, code 4 changed meaning. It was Selvmord until 31 December 1990 and Drab/vold from 1 January 1991. dodsaars runs from 1970 to 2001 and so contains both, in one column, with nothing to tell them apart except the date of death. Reading code 4 as one thing across the whole register counts homicides as suicides or the reverse. Codes 6 (Drab/vold) and 9 (Uoplyst) belong only to the old set and stop at the end of 1990; codes 3 and 5 only start in 1991.

c_dodsmaade_2002.name: Doedsmaade, 2002 onwards (DAR t_dodsaarsag_2)
c_dodsmaade_2002.description: How the person died, as coded from 2002. A different set of numbers from the one used until 2001, for the same five concepts. Nothing marks the change in the data itself: the column has the same name in both registers.
c_dodsmaade_2002.note: This is the set behind the `c_dodsmaade` column in dodsaasg, and the numbers do not mean what the same numbers mean in `dodsaars`. There, under `c_dodsmaade`, 1 is Naturlig død, 2 is Ulykke and 5 is Uoplyst. Here 1 is Voldshandling, 2 is Selvmord and 5 is Naturlig død. A study that spans 2001 and 2002 is reading two different code sets out of two columns with the same name, and every value maps to something plausible in the other set, so nothing looks wrong. A blank is a registration error, not a missing manner of death.

c_dodssted.note: All five codes are valid from 1 January 2002. The variable says nothing about deaths before that, which is the whole period dodsaars covers.

c_udm.description: How the contact ended and where the patient went. Only four codes cover the whole register; the rest each have their own window, and the way a discharge to another hospital unit is coded changes completely at the end of 2003.

Codes 2, 4, 7 and A only begin in 1995, E in 2002, and K and L in 2006.

diagtype.note: The guide long described this as an A/B/G column. There are six codes, and three of them stop: **G runs 1995-2003 only**, M 1998-2013 and C 2002-2013. A and B run the whole period, H from 1995. So a comorbidity definition built on G silently covers nine years and nothing else, and filtering to A/B/G drops referral diagnoses entirely. Which types to keep is a case definition, not a technicality: outcomes usually use A and B. Carry the type column into the extract so the definition can be varied later.

disco_old.note: Do not read a code here against DISCO-08's published list (disco08.yaml): the two classifications share the general numeric shape but DST revised the detail at the 2010 switch, and a code that means one occupation in DISCO-08 is not guaranteed to mean the same thing, or to exist at all, in the pre-2010 scheme.

Not the occupation itself, only where that code came from, which matters because DST states code quality is best when this is 1, 2, 4 or 10, and worse for the other, imputation-based values.
discotyp.note: A different question from the DISCO occupation code itself: this says where that code came from, not what the job was. DST's own page states that DISCO code quality is best when discotyp is 1, 2, 4 or 10, and that the remaining codes mean the DISCO code was set by imputation.

herkomst.name: Herkomst (origin)
herkomst.description: Whether a person is of Danish origin, an immigrant or a descendant. Derived from the person's own and the parents' birthplace and citizenship.
herkomst.note: A descendant is born in Denmark: neither parent is both a Danish citizen and born in Denmark. So the category says something about the parents, not about where the person was born, and it does not change over a lifetime the way citizenship does.

hfaudd.name: DISCED-15 AUDD (completed education)
hfaudd.description: The code for a completed education under DISCED-15. Four digits identifying which education, not how long or how high it is. DISCED-15 has a separate code for an ongoing or interrupted education (UDD).
hfaudd.note: This is an identifier, not a scale. The level (short, medium, long) has to be looked up in a separate table, and cannot be read off the digits: 4112 is an electrician, and taking the first two digits as a level code makes it a long higher education. DST documents the ongoing-education codes separately as DISCED-15 UDD.

hustype.name: Husstandstype
hustype.description: The type of household a person lives in.

icd10.name: ICD-10 (WHO form)
icd10.description: Diagnosis codes in the plain WHO form, letter followed by digits, with no prefix: E119 rather than DE119. This is what the cause-of-death registers hold. The patient registers hold the D-prefixed SKS form instead, which is `icd10_sks`.
icd10.note: Do not strip a leading D from these codes. The habit comes from LPR, where the D is really there, and applying it here removes the first character of a real code: E119 becomes 119, which matches nothing and raises no error. The danger is worst where a code genuinely begins with D. ICD-10 chapter D covers in-situ and benign neoplasms, so D46 is myelodysplastic syndrome, a whole code. Strip its "prefix" and you get 46, which looks like a code and is not one.

icd10_sks.name: ICD-10, Danish SKS form (D-prefixed)
icd10_sks.description: Diagnosis codes as the patient registers store them: the WHO code with the letter D in front, so WHO's E11 appears as DE11. This is an LPR form, not a property of Danish ICD-10 in general. The cause-of-death registers store the plain WHO code and use `icd10` instead.
icd10_sks.note: The D prefix is a Danish addition, not part of the WHO code. Matching WHO codes directly against LPR without allowing for it returns nothing. Do not carry the habit across to the cause-of-death registers: they hold the plain code, so stripping a D there removes the first real character instead.

icd8.name: ICD-8
icd8.description: Diagnosis codes as the patient registers stored them before 1994. Pure digits, no letter and no decimal point, so 446.30 is written 44630. Nothing about them looks like ICD-10, which is what makes them easy to mistake for a broken column rather than a different classification.
icd8.note: A study whose period starts before 1994 is reading two classifications out of one column. ICD-10 codes match nothing in the early years, and the usual substr(c_diag, 2, 4) returns a meaningless fragment of an ICD-8 code rather than failing, so nothing tells you it went wrong.
icd8.source_name: Retired classification, no current DST page

ie_type.name: IE-type (herkomst)
ie_type.description: Whether a person is of Danish origin, an immigrant or a descendant.
ie_type.note: DST's current high-quality page for IE_TYPE states that the variable has no value set. The codes here come from the older TIMES3 archive page, which does publish them.

indm.name: Indlaeggelsesmaade (LPR2 c_indm)
indm.description: Whether the contact was acute or planned. Three codes, one of which was discontinued.
indm.note: From 2014 this is what separates an emergency-room visit from an ordinary outpatient one, because `c_pattype` code `3` was discontinued and both arrive as `2`. Code `9` (Uoplyst) stops at the end of 2003, so a missing value after that is genuinely missing rather than coded as unknown.

indud_kode.name: Indud_kode (migration direction)
indud_kode.description: Whether a migration event is an immigration or an emigration.
indud_kode.note: Use `U` for censoring at emigration. People who never emigrated have no `U` event at all, so they are simply absent rather than carrying a missing date. Two caveats from the guide: CPR only has complete immigration and emigration data from 1971, so someone who immigrated before that has no event and looks resident since birth; and a move to Greenland is a status of its own in CPR rather than an emigration. Confirm the values on your own delivery.

koen.name: Køn (sex)
koen.description: Sex as coded in BEF. Small enumerated set.
koen.note: DST's classification KOEN_V1_1980 also defines `9` for not stated, which a delivery may not contain but a value set should. Sex is taken from the tenth digit of the CPR number: even is female, odd is male.

kom.name: Kommunekode (municipality code)
kom.description: Municipality of residence. Three-digit codes. 98 municipalities since the 2007 reform, which replaced the previous 271. Christiansø (411) is not under a municipality but administered directly by the state.
kom.note: These codes are valid from 1 January 2007. A study reaching further back needs the pre-reform classification, where the same number can mean a different municipality - confirmed for two reused codes against a current-only DST source: 707 is Norddjurs today, not its pre-2007 meaning, and likewise 849 is Jammerbugt. `lookup:` below covers only this post-2007 set (99 entries), not the full 278-code `values_from` file. Christiansø (411) is included in `lookup:` even though it is not a municipality (see description above): it is a real value a `kom` column can hold, and DST's own current-only classification lists it as its own area code alongside the 98 municipalities. Excluding it would just move the "unhandled code" problem this fix is meant to solve onto that one value.

kont_type.name: Contact type (LPR3 kont_type)
kont_type.description: The LPR3 contact type. Documented as SKS codes rather than the single digits LPR2 used, so the values look nothing like LPR2's c_pattype and cannot be mapped across one to one. In practice the column holds BOTH, and which one a row holds is decided by `lprindberetningssystem`, not by the year: rows reported through LPR3 carry the SKS codes, rows reported through MiniPAS carry LPR2 patient types (`0` and `2`, see the `pattype` code system). Both were present as late as 2024 in a delivery checked in 2026.
kont_type.note: `ALCA00` means physical attendance, which is the closest LPR3 gets to LPR2's inpatient flag. It marks attendance, not admission, so a study that treats it as "was admitted" will include outpatient visits. Check what your own delivery holds before filtering: single digits and SKS codes have been seen side by side in the same year, so `kont_type == "ALCA00"` can silently drop rows that are the same kind of contact recorded in the other form. Cross-tabulate it against `lprindberetningssystem` first. MiniPAS was the route private providers reported through, so the two forms are not only two notations, they are also two different parts of the health service.

lprindberetningssystem.name: Reporting system (LPR_A lprindberetningssystem)
lprindberetningssystem.description: Which historical reporting-system generation a lpr_a_kontakt, lpr_a_diagnose or lpr_a_procregistrering row was originally reported through. Do not confuse this with LPR_F vs LPR_A: that is a choice of DELIVERY FORMAT (which files you even read, kontakter/diagnoser/forloeb vs lpr_a_kontakt/lpr_a_diagnose), decided before you open a file. This column is a value INSIDE the LPR_A files, telling you which of several older reporting systems' migrated history a given row within LPR_A came from, since lpr_a_kontakt is a single consolidated table holding migrated history as well as current LPR3 reporting. See [LPR_A vs LPR_F ->](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr-a-format).
lprindberetningssystem.note: Confirm the exact strings with `count(lprindberetningssystem)` before relying on "LPR2" or "LPR1" in a filter: they are well-established as concepts in this guide, but nobody has pasted the literal value back from DARTER the way pitfall 5 did for "LPR3". "MiniPAS" is safe to rely on, since kont_type.yaml's coalescing logic already depends on it being exactly that string. This column is unrelated to LPR_F vs LPR_A: that choice is made before you open a file, this one lives inside the file you already chose.
lprindberetningssystem.source_name: No DST/Sundhedsdatastyrelsen kodeark for this column exists; the value set below is reconstructed from DARTER-team-confirmed facts already established elsewhere in this guide (this pitfalls page, and kont_type.yaml), not from a published code list.

Stable across the LPR3 cutover, unlike ProcedureType (see mfr_procedure_type.yaml).
mfr_diagnose_type.note: When DiagnoseType is "+", DiagnoseKode is an add-on that only makes sense attached to another diagnosis: that parent diagnosis, its own type, and whether it was later disproven live in DiagnoseKode_Parent, DiagnoseType_Parent and SenereAfkraeftet_Parent on the same row, not in DiagnoseKode itself. `tobaksforbrug`'s DUT* codes and `mfr_fosterpraesentation`'s DUP* codes are exactly this kind of "+" add-on code before the LPR3 cutover.
mfr_diagnose_type.source_name: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen: Dokumentation af Fødselsregisteret 2019 og frem, sheet Kolonner

mfr_er_cprnummer_gyldigt.name: ErCPRnummerGyldigt (MFR 2019+, CPR-number validity type)
mfr_er_cprnummer_gyldigt.description: What kind of number sits in CPRnummer_Barn / CPRnummer_Mor / CPRnummer_Far in the 2019+ Medical Birth Register: a real, currently active CPR-number, one that used to be valid, a stand-in issued for someone the CPR system cannot yet or can no longer resolve, a known test number, or something else. Shared code across all three person columns.
mfr_er_cprnummer_gyldigt.note: Only "Gyldig hos CPR" is guaranteed to resolve when joining to `bef` or any other CPR-keyed register: an "Udgået hos CPR" number identifies a real person but under a number CPR itself has since retired (e.g. after a birth-date correction), while "Erstatnings CPR" and "Fiktivt" numbers were never real CPR-numbers at all and will join to nothing. Check this column before joining CPRnummer_Barn, _Mor, or _Far onwards, rather than assuming every value in those columns is a working key.

mfr_foedested_faktisk.name: Foedested_Faktisk (MFR 2019+, actual place of birth)
mfr_foedested_faktisk.description: Where the child was actually born (as opposed to which institution reported the birth). A DST-local derived classification, not a raw SKS code: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen computes it from a mix of the SKS result code RGAE* (rows reported through LPR3) and the birth diagnosis code (FoedselsDiagnose_Barn, DZ38*/DZ381*/etc, for older or paper-reported rows), with several source-specific rules layered on top. See provenance for the exact derivation, which changes at the LPR3 cutover (Feb/March 2019) and again at a 2012 boundary within the pre-LPR3 period.
mfr_foedested_faktisk.note: Do not try to derive this yourself from FoedselsDiagnose_Barn alone: the mapping from birth-diagnosis code to actual birthplace changed at two different boundaries (2012, and the LPR3 cutover in Feb/March 2019), and Sundhedsdatastyrelsen has already resolved that history into this single column. Recomputing it from the diagnosis code with only the current (post-2019) mapping will misclassify pre-2012 home births as "outside hospital, birth clinic and home".
mfr_foedested_faktisk.source_name: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen: Dokumentation af Fødselsregisteret 2019 og frem, sheet Kolonner

mfr_fosterpraesentation.name: Fosterpraesentation (MFR, fetal presentation at birth)
mfr_fosterpraesentation.description: The child's position in the uterus during birth, as coded in the Medical Birth Register (Nyfoedte.Fosterpraesentation, and the Barn satellite tables). Same dual-prefix pattern as `tobaksforbrug`: DUP* is a diagnosis add-on code used before the LPR3 cutover (Feb/March 2019), RGAD* is a result code (result type RDA34) used from that cutover on. The numeric suffix is identical across both, only the prefix changed.
mfr_fosterpraesentation.note: Recorded on the child's own fødselskontakt (or as an add-on to it before LPR3), not the mother's, even though fetal presentation is clinically a fact about the pregnancy and delivery. Join through DW_EK_Nyfoedt if cross-referencing against Barn_* satellite tables, not DW_EK_Foedsel.
mfr_fosterpraesentation.source_name: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen: SKS Browser, classification res.praesent / dia DUP (fosterpræsentation)

mfr_kilde_barn.name: Kilde_Barn (MFR 2019+, source of the child's birth record)
mfr_kilde_barn.description: Which of the three data sources produced this newborn's row in the 2019+ Medical Birth Register (Nyfoedte.Kilde_Barn): the hospital reporting system, or one of two paper forms for cases the reporting system does not reach. Narrower than the parents' Kilde_Mor/Kilde_Far code, which has two extra values ("from CPR" and "not stated") that do not apply to the child's own birth record - see `mfr_kilde_forael` for those.
mfr_kilde_barn.note: This value gates which other columns are populated at all. `DW_EK_Kontakt_Barn` is only set when this is "1"; `DW_ID_Hjem_Barn` only when this is "2"; and `DW_ID_Doed_Barn` when this is "3" (or when a paper stillbirth form supplements an LPR3 birth record). A join to `Barn_Kontakter` or any other LPR-sourced satellite table will silently return nothing for rows where Kilde_Barn is "2" or "3", since those children have no LPR contact at all.
mfr_kilde_barn.source_name: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen: Dokumentation af Fødselsregisteret 2019 og frem, sheet Kolonner

mfr_kilde_forael.name: Kilde_Mor / Kilde_Far (MFR 2019+, source of the parent's record)
mfr_kilde_forael.description: Which data source a parent's information came from in the 2019+ Medical Birth Register (Nyfoedte.Kilde_Mor, Kilde_Far). Shared code between mother and father: both columns document the identical five values. Wider than the child's own Kilde_Barn code, which lacks "from CPR" and "not stated" since a birth always has a determinable source but a parent's identity sometimes does not.
mfr_kilde_forael.note: "9 = Uoplyst" exists for a parent (most often the father) but has no counterpart on the child's own Kilde_Barn: a birth with no determinable source simply is not in the register at all. Treat Kilde_Far == "9" as a real, common case (unknown paternity), not a data-quality flag to filter out.
mfr_kilde_forael.source_name: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen: Dokumentation af Fødselsregisteret 2019 og frem, sheet Kolonner

mfr_koen.name: Koen (MFR 2019+, letter code)
mfr_koen.description: Sex as coded in the 2019+ Medical Birth Register (Nyfoedte.Koen_Barn, Koen_Mor, Koen_Far). Not the same encoding as `koen`: that is DST's numeric KOEN_V1_1980 classification (1/2/9), this is Sundhedsdatastyrelsen's own letter code for this register family. Same concept, different authority, different literal values - do not assume a column typed against one resolves against the other.
mfr_koen.note: For the child, this is derived from Dim.Borger.KoenID plus, for stillbirths reported on paper, the stillbirth form or the CPR-like number itself - not purely a CPR lookup, since a stillborn child may never receive one. For the mother and father, it is a straight lookup on their own CPR-derived sex, so Koen_Far being "Ukendt" or missing does not imply anything about the birth itself, only that paternal identity was not established.
mfr_koen.source_name: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen: Dokumentation af Fødselsregisteret 2019 og frem, sheet Kolonner

mfr_levendefoedt_doedfoedt.name: LevendefoedtDoedfoedt (MFR 2019+, live birth vs stillbirth)
mfr_levendefoedt_doedfoedt.description: Whether the row in the 2019+ Medical Birth Register is a live birth or a stillbirth. The DST 1997-2018 "Levendefødte" table (`mfr.yaml`) only ever held live births, so this column is new: the 2019+ Nyfoedte table unifies both outcomes into one table for the first time.
mfr_levendefoedt_doedfoedt.note: A query written against the old 1997-2018 "Levendefødte" table implicitly filtered to live births by construction. The same query pointed at `mfr_nyfoedte` without `LevendefoedtDoedfoedt == 1` will silently pull in stillbirths too. Apgarscore is set to 0 for every stillbirth rather than left missing, which will also distort a naive mean/summary of Apgar scores computed without this filter.
mfr_levendefoedt_doedfoedt.source_name: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen: Dokumentation af Fødselsregisteret 2019 og frem, sheet Kolonner

mfr_procedure_type.name: ProcedureType (MFR 2019+ satellite tables)
mfr_procedure_type.description: What role a procedure code plays on a Barn_Procedurer/Mor_Procedurer row. Reorganised at the LPR3 cutover: before it, a three-way split of surgical operation roles (partial/main-in-procedure/main-in-contact); after it, a two-way split of indication vs procedure. Code "P" survives the cutover but changes meaning, the same trap as `pattype` and `c_dodsmaade`.
mfr_procedure_type.note: Reading "P" as one stable category across the whole table conflates "the main operation" (pre-LPR3, one of three specific operation roles) with "any procedure at all" (post-LPR3, the default value for most rows). This will inflate counts of "main operations" for LPR3-era rows if not checked against IndberetningsSystem first. See ProcedureType_Parent for the narrower set of types (post-LPR3: only "P"; pre-LPR3: D/P/V) that a "+" add-on can actually attach to.
mfr_procedure_type.source_name: Sundhedsdatastyrelsen: Dokumentation af Fødselsregisteret 2019 og frem, sheet Kolonner

nace_db07.name: DB07 brancheklassifikation (industry, NACE Rev.2)
nace_db07.description: Danish industry classification DB07, aligned with EU NACE Rev.2, current from 2007-2008. Hierarchical: level 1 is a small set of broad sections, level 2 the detailed code.
nace_db07.note: Two things to check before using this as a lookup. First, format: this file writes the detailed code with dots (01.11.00); nace_db07 and nace_db07_13 hold it without them (011100). Second, coverage: checked against nace_db07's own value list on DST's high-quality variable page, only 490 of its 743 distinct codes match this file's 738 level-2 codes even after stripping dots. As with DISCO-08 (see disco08.yaml), the industry code for a given person-year can be sourced from more than one register, so a code absent from this CSV is not necessarily an error.

nace_old.name: NACE brancheklassifikation, foer DB07 (2007)
nace_old.description: Industry of a person's main employment, before the 2007-2008 switch to DB07/NACE Rev.2. No published value list has been found for this revision, only its successor's.
nace_old.note: Do not read a code here against DB07/NACE Rev.2's published list (nace_db07.yaml): the 2007-2008 revision changed the code structure, and a code that means one industry under DB07 is not guaranteed to mean the same thing, or to exist at all, under this older scheme.

nystgr.name: Stillingsgruppering, 1980-1995 (AKM)
nystgr.description: A four-digit occupation/position grouping used before DISCO. The first digit marks the broad labour-market position (self-employed, employee, out of the labour force and so on), the rest the specific occupation within it.
nystgr.note: Retired in 1995 and replaced by DISCO. A code's meaning can shift within the window a study covers: DST's own page notes that code 5100 changed meaning in 1992 (the group it now names used code 5500 before that year), so a series spanning 1992 needs the year-by-year note on the source page, not just the current label.

omfang.name: Omfang af skattepligt (AKM/Indkomst)
omfang.description: How fully a person's tax and income data cover the year: fully liable both 1 January and 31 December, moved during the year, died during the year, a child with no income, or one of a few edge cases the tax and settlement registers cannot reconcile. Not a demographic fact about the person, an administrative fact about how complete their income record is.
omfang.note: Code 2 changed meaning at the 2002 boundary: before 2002 (and again 2002-2009) it also absorbed children under 15 with no income or wealth, a group that codes 0 and 4 cover separately in other years. Code 5 (died, not settled) only exists from 2002; before that, a death with no settled income was coded 2 instead. DST does not publish exact boundary dates for this drift the way it does for codes 0 and 3 (see above), so treat "2002" as DST's own rounding, not a verified cutover date. DST's own publications and statistikbanktabeller are restricted to omfang=1: an analysis that does not filter on it silently includes partial-year residents, the newly dead, and unsettled records alongside ordinary full-year taxpayers.

oprart.name: Procedureart (LPR2 c_oprart)
oprart.description: What role a procedure code plays on the contact: the main one, a sub-procedure or an add-on code.
oprart.note: Counting rows in the procedure table counts add-on codes and sub-procedures as procedures. If you want one row per operation, filter to `V` or `P` first. All four codes run from 1996 with no breaks.

values.en: Main procedure of the completed contact

pattype.name: Patienttype (LPR2 c_pattype)
pattype.description: The patient's administrative relationship to the hospital. LPR2 only: LPR3 has no equivalent, and the type has to be derived from contact duration plus an acute marker.
pattype.note: There are four codes, not six, and three of them changed meaning. Code `1` was Dagpatient until 1986 and Deldoegnspatient from 1987, and then stops entirely at the end of 2001. Code `2` was Natpatient until 1986 and Ambulant from 1987. Code `0` was Heldoegnspatient until 2001 and Indlagt patient from 2002. The register only started using `1`, `2` and `3` in 1994, so before that essentially every contact is `0`. Code `3` was discontinued at the end of 2013, and from 2014 an emergency-room visit arrives as `2` with an acute admission mode in `c_indm`. Reading `2` as outpatient across the whole register therefore mislabels night patients before 1987 and emergency visits after 2013.

plads.name: Familiestatus (plads i familien)
plads.description: A person's position in the family.

reg.name: Region
reg.description: Region of residence. The five regions created by the 2007 municipal reform, plus a code for unknown.
reg.note: Do not confuse these with AMT, the pre-2007 counties, which has 16 codes in the ranges 11-14, 21-24, 31-37 and 88. Different geography, different era.

sex_lpr.name: Koen in LPR2 (c_sex)
sex_lpr.description: Sex as recorded on a hospital contact. Not the same coding as BEF's `koen`, and not the same coding across the register's own lifetime.
sex_lpr.note: The coding changed at the start of 2005: `1`/`2` until the end of 2004, `M`/`K` from 2005. A study spanning that year that filters on `c_sex == "2"` keeps only the women seen before 2005 and silently drops the rest, with no error and no empty result to warn you. Take sex from BEF instead, where it is `koen` coded `1`/`2` throughout, unless you specifically need what the hospital recorded.

sks.name: SKS procedure codes
sks.description: Sundhedsvaesenets Klassifikations System. The procedure branch of the same classification that supplies diagnosis codes, used in LPR_SKSOPR and LPR_SKSUBE. Surgical procedures sit under K, examinations and other non-surgical procedures under the remaining letters.
sks.note: The codes are hierarchical, so a prefix match selects a whole branch. That also makes it easy to select more than you meant: check how many characters your intended group actually needs before filtering with starts_with().

socio13.name: Socioøkonomisk klassifikation (SOCIO13)
socio13.description: Socioeconomic position: what a person mainly lived on during the year. The codes are hierarchical, so the first digit is the broad group and the third the detail.
socio13.note: Two codes are easy to misread. `410` is **Andre** (other), not unemployed: the unemployed are `210`. And `420` is **children under 15**, a known category rather than a missing value, so it appearing in an adult cohort means the index date is wrong rather than the data being incomplete.

tobaksforbrug.name: Tobaksforbrug / rygestatus (MFR, mother's smoking status in pregnancy)
tobaksforbrug.description: The mother's tobacco use during pregnancy, as coded in the Medical Birth Register (Nyfoedte.Tobaksforbrug, and the Mor satellite tables). Two SKS code families cover the exact same nine categories: DUT* is a diagnosis add-on code, used for rows reported before the LPR3 cutover in Feb/March 2019; RGAB* is a result code (result type RDA25), used from that cutover on. The numeric suffix is identical across both (DUT20 and RGAB20 mean the same thing), only the prefix and reporting mechanism changed.
tobaksforbrug.note: Bliddal et al. 2018 (mined earlier for this guide) reports smoking status as 100% missing before late 1997 and notes the field is otherwise reliably recorded once it exists. That predates both DUT and RGAB: an analysis spanning multiple decades needs to know smoking status went through at least two encodings (pre-1997: absent; 1997 to the LPR3 cutover: DUT*; LPR3 cutover onwards: RGAB*), not one stable variable. When multiple smoking-status sources exist for the same birth, Sundhedsdatastyrelsen resolves them in a fixed order (result/add-on tied to the primary birth record over other records, "komplet" over "inkomplet" reporting status, then the heaviest smoking category over lighter ones) - see the MFR 2019+ documentation for the exact tie-break rules if you need to reproduce Tobaksforbrug from the underlying satellite tables yourself.

akm.name: Arbejdsklassifikationsmodulet (labour classification module)
akm.description: One record per person per year with their socioeconomic classification: employed, self-employed, student, unemployed, pensioner, outside the labour market.
akm.grain: one row per person per period

bef.name: Befolkningen (population register)
bef.description: Status register with one snapshot per person per reference time point. Delivered quarterly since 2008 (March, June, September, December); December only before that, so the cadence is not constant across the coverage.
bef.grain: one row per person per period

cancer.name: Cancerregisteret
cancer.description: One row per incident cancer diagnosis: a person appears once per tumour, not once in total. Running since 1943, which makes it one of the longest continuous cancer registries in the world.

dod.name: Døde i Danmark (deaths in Denmark)
dod.description: One row per deceased person. This is the register to use for date of death, and it covers the whole period on its own.

dodsaars.name: Dødsårssagsregistret
dodsaars.description: Cause of death for 1970-2001. Closed. It also carries a date of death, which is why it is so often used for censoring, but that use is a mistake for any study running past 2001.

dodsaarsager.name: Dødsårsagsregister (2022-)
dodsaarsager.description: Cause of death from 2022. The current register, and the third naming scheme the chain has used.

dodsaasg.name: Dødsårsagsregister (2002-2022)
dodsaasg.description: Cause of death for 2002-2022. Closed. Takes over from DODSAARS and is itself replaced by DODSAARSAGER.

faik.name: Familieindkomster (family income)
faik.description: Household income per year, keyed on the household rather than the person. Reaching it from a person means going through BEF for the familie_id.
faik.grain: one row per family per year

ftbarn.name: FTBARN - Fertilitet: børn
ftbarn.description: One row per child (live-born or stillborn) in Denmark, 1973-2023. Distinct from mfr_nyfoedte: this is a demography/population-statistics register (parent linkage, adoption status, birth registration source), not a clinical record of the birth itself - it carries only a handful of clinical facts (weight, length, live/stillbirth) sourced from MFR.

ftforael.name: FTFORAEL - Fertilitet: forælder
ftforael.description: One row per parent-child link in Denmark, 1973-2023: up to two rows per child in ftbarn (mother and father), distinguished by MOR_FAR. Carries four different parity and birth-spacing measures per parent (DEMOGRAFISK_/ENKELT_/FAMILIE_/MEDICINSK_), a demography-specific distinction DST's own page does not further define - see the reader_note.
ftforael.joins: PNR to FTBARN (many-to-one); FORAELDER_PNR to BEF (many-to-one)

ftnaevn.name: FTNAEVN - Fertilitet: Nævner
ftnaevn.description: One row per person per year, 1973-2023, giving that person's exposure time and status within reproductive age for that year - the denominator used to compute fertility rates (ANDEL: proportion of the year spent in fertile age). Not restricted to parents in ftbarn/ftforael: this is a broader population-exposure table, not a birth-event table.
ftnaevn.grain: one row per person per period

lab_dm_forsker.name: Laboratoriedatabasens Forskertabel
lab_dm_forsker.description: One row per laboratory result attached to a request: a blood or other sample, its analyte code, the result and its unit. Very large - well over a billion rows - so filter before collecting.

lmdb.name: Lægemiddeldatabasen (prescription register)
lmdb.description: One row per dispensed prescription, so the same person appears many times. Covers prescriptions dispensed at community pharmacies.

lpr_a_betalingsoplysninger.name: LPR_A_BETALINGSOPLYSNINGER - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - Betalingsoplysninger
lpr_a_betalingsoplysninger.description: One row per set of payment/billing information for a contact, or for a procedure that has its own separate payer. A payment-information set covers three facts: the payment agreement (ALFA-codes), the payer (ALFB-codes), and the specialisation level (ALFC-codes). No unique key: a row hangs on the contact or procedure it was registered on.
lpr_a_betalingsoplysninger.joins: DW_EK_KONTAKT to LPR_A_KONTAKT (many-to-one); DW_EK_PROCEDUREREGISTRERING to LPR_A_PROCREGISTRERING (many-to-one)

lpr_a_diagnose.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - diagnoseoplysning
lpr_a_diagnose.description: One row per diagnosis on a contact. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_a_kontakt on dw_ek_kontakt to reach the person.
lpr_a_diagnose.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_a_forloeb.name: LPR_A_FORLOEB - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - forloeb
lpr_a_forloeb.description: One row per LPR3 course element ("forloebselement") for the whole population, not restricted to birth-related courses the way mfr_barn_forloeb/mfr_mor_forloeb are. Contacts (lpr_a_kontakt) reference a course element from this table via DW_EK_FORLOEB.
lpr_a_forloeb.joins: PNR to BEF (many-to-one); DW_EK_FORLOEB to LPR_A_KONTAKT (one-to-many)

lpr_a_forloebsmarkoer.name: LPR_A_FORLOEBSMARKOER - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - Forloebsmarkoerer
lpr_a_forloebsmarkoer.description: One row per course marker: a timestamped event within a health course (helbredsforloeb), such as "referred for diagnostic workup", "informed consent given", or "specialised rehabilitation ended". Used for tracking wait times and deadlines under Denmark's "ret til hurtig udredning" (right to fast diagnostic workup) and cancer-pathway rules. No unique key: a marker "hangs" on the course it belongs to via dw_ek_forloeb.

lpr_a_henvisning_tillaeg.name: LPR_A_HENVISNING_TILLAEG - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - Henvisning_tillaeg
lpr_a_henvisning_tillaeg.description: One row per addendum code to a referral reason (henvisningsaarsag) registered on a contact or a course. Reporting a referral reason is generally voluntary in LPR3 (regions/municipalities may require it locally), so this table can be empty or near-empty depending on delivery year. No unique key: a row hangs on the contact or course it was registered on.
lpr_a_henvisning_tillaeg.joins: DW_EK_FORLOEB to LPR_A_FORLOEB (many-to-one); DW_EK_KONTAKT to LPR_A_KONTAKT (many-to-one)

lpr_a_kontakt.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - kontaktoplysninger
lpr_a_kontakt.description: One row per hospital contact. Carries pnr, so the diagnosis and procedure tables reach the person through it. DST gives the coverage as 2017-2025: the table reaches back before the March 2019 LPR3 boundary because outpatient contacts already held in LPR2 were folded into it.

lpr_a_kontaktlokation.name: LPR_A_KONTAKTLOKATION - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - Kontaktlokationer
lpr_a_kontaktlokation.description: One row per contact location: where the citizen officially stayed at a given time during a physical-attendance contact (kontakttype ALCA00). Reporting a contact location is mandatory for physical-attendance contacts. A contact can have several locations if the citizen is moved during it while responsibility stays with the same SOR unit, and a location can also carry an absence/leave code when the citizen holds a bed but is not physically present. No unique key: a row hangs on the contact it was registered on.

lpr_a_mor_barn_relation.name: LPR_A_MOR_BARN_RELATION - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - mor/barn-relation
lpr_a_mor_barn_relation.description: One row per linked mother-child pair of LPR3 course elements around a birth. The DST-documented mechanism for finding the mother's course element that corresponds to a given child's, and vice versa.
lpr_a_mor_barn_relation.joins: PNR_BARN to BEF (many-to-one); PNR_MOR to BEF (many-to-one); PNR_BARN to MFR_NYFOEDTE (one-to-one)

lpr_a_procregistrering.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - procedureregistreringer
lpr_a_procregistrering.description: One row per procedure registration. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_a_kontakt on dw_ek_kontakt, exactly as the diagnosis table does.
lpr_a_procregistrering.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_a_procregistrering_aflys.name: LPR_A_PROCREGISTRERING_AFLYS - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - Aflyste procedureregistreringer
lpr_a_procregistrering_aflys.description: One row per procedure registration that was cancelled/withdrawn rather than carried out, mirroring lpr_a_procregistrering's column structure (parent/child procedure codes, timestamps, producing unit). Not a subset of lpr_a_procregistrering: a cancelled procedure registration is not expected to also appear there.
lpr_a_procregistrering_aflys.joins: DW_EK_FORLOEB to LPR_A_FORLOEB (many-to-one); DW_EK_KONTAKT to LPR_A_KONTAKT (many-to-one); DW_SK_SYGEHUSOPHOLD to LPR_A_SGHOPHOLD (many-to-one)

lpr_a_resultater.name: LPR_A_RESULTATER - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - Oplysninger om resultatindberetninger
lpr_a_resultater.description: One row per mandatory result report (resultatindberetning): a report required to a specific external registry or purpose, triggered by a specific value elsewhere in the LPR3 reporting (e.g. a cancer diagnosis triggers a required cancer-registry report, trigger type "Diagnose", trigger code "RAA01"). Replaces LPR2's mandatory addendum coding, which used to live as an addendum to a diagnosis/procedure, in the accident variables/table, or in the birth table. No unique key: a row hangs on the contact or course it was registered against.
lpr_a_resultater.joins: DW_EK_FORLOEB to LPR_A_FORLOEB (many-to-one); DW_EK_KONTAKT to LPR_A_KONTAKT (many-to-one); DW_EK_PROCEDUREREGISTRERING to LPR_A_PROCREGISTRERING (many-to-one)

lpr_a_sghophold.name: LPR_A_SGHOPHOLD - Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - sygehusophold
lpr_a_sghophold.description: One row per hospital stay, grouping the contacts (lpr_a_kontakt) that belong to one continuous admission episode. ANTAL_KONT_SGH_OPH gives how many contacts were grouped into it.
lpr_a_sghophold.joins: PNR to BEF (many-to-one); DW_EK_KONTAKT_FOERSTE to LPR_A_KONTAKT (one-to-one)

lpr_adm.name: Landspatientregistret - administrative oplysninger
lpr_adm.description: One row per hospital contact. This is the only LPR2 dataset that carries pnr, so every other one reaches the person through it.

lpr_afl.name: Landspatientregistret - aflyste operationer
lpr_afl.description: One row per operation that was planned and then cancelled, so it was never actually carried out. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.
lpr_afl.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_bes.name: LPR_BES - Landspatientregistret - ambulante besoegsdatoer
lpr_bes.description: One row per outpatient (ambulant) visit date. A single contact (lpr_adm/recnum) can have several outpatient visits over its course, each with its own row here. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.
lpr_bes.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_diag.name: Landspatientregistret - diagnoser
lpr_diag.description: One row per diagnosis on a contact, so a contact can have several. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.
lpr_diag.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_foedsler.name: LPR_FOEDSLER - Landspatientregistret - foedsler
lpr_foedsler.description: One row per birth-related contact, with maternity-specific facts (parity, antenatal visit counts, the newborn's weight and length). Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person - the mother, since the newborn is not necessarily a person with their own contact here.

lpr_opr.name: LPR_OPR - Landspatientregistret - operationer efter ICD8 klassifikationen
lpr_opr.description: One row per operation coded under the pre-1996 (ICD8-era) classification. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person. Use lpr_sksopr.yaml instead for operations under the modern SKS coding used from 1996 onwards.
lpr_opr.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_pas.name: Landspatientregistret - passiv ventetid
lpr_pas.description: One row per period of passive waiting time (ventetid patienten selv har forlaenget, fx ved udsaettelse), with a reason, its start/end dates, and which department/hospital the patient returned to when active treatment resumed. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.
lpr_pas.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_sksopr.name: Landspatientregistret - operationer
lpr_sksopr.description: One row per surgical procedure. Carries no pnr and no admission date: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.
lpr_sksopr.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_sksube.name: Landspatientregistret - undersoegelser og behandlinger
lpr_sksube.description: One row per examination or treatment. Structured exactly like LPR_SKSOPR, and joined to lpr_adm on recnum in the same way.
lpr_sksube.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_udtilsgh.name: LPR_UDTILSGH - Landspatientregistret - oplysninger om sygehus og afdeling
lpr_udtilsgh.description: One row per contact recording the hospital and department the patient was discharged (transferred) to. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.

lpr_ulyk.name: LPR_ULYK - Landspatientregistret - ulykkeskoder
lpr_ulyk.description: One row per accident/injury code on a contact. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person. Before 2000, the equivalent accident variables (c_eakt/c_emek/c_epart/c_emodpart/c_ested/c_etraf) are documented as living directly on lpr_adm rather than in this table - check whether lpr_adm carries them for a project's specific delivery before assuming this table is the only source.
lpr_ulyk.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_vente.name: Landspatientregistret - ventetid
lpr_vente.description: One row per waiting-time period tied to a contact, with a status and a start/end date. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person. This concept and table name are read from the column names alone; no institutional description was found.
lpr_vente.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

mfr.name: MFR - Levendefoedte fra det medicinske foedselsregister
mfr.description: One row per live birth, carrying both the mother and the child. A mother appears once per birth, so the register is keyed on the child rather than the person. DST cuts several other datasets from the same underlying register (stillbirths, pregnancy complications, home births and more); this is only the live-births one.

mfr_barn_diagnoser.name: Barn_Diagnoser - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_barn_diagnoser.description: One row per diagnosis, contact reason, or diagnosis add-on code for the child, tied to a contact starting within 42 days of birth. Structurally the same idea as lpr_a_diagnose. `tobaksforbrug`'s DUT* codes and `mfr_fosterpraesentation`'s DUP* codes, before the LPR3 cutover, are add-on rows in this exact table (DiagnoseType = "+").
mfr_barn_diagnoser.joins: DW_EK_Nyfoedt to MFR_NYFOEDTE (many-to-one); DW_EK_Kontakt to MFR_BARN_KONTAKTER (many-to-one); DW_EK_Forloeb to MFR_BARN_FORLOEB (many-to-one)

mfr_barn_forloeb.name: Barn_Forloeb - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_barn_forloeb.description: One row per LPR course element ("forloebselement") for the child, linked to a contact starting within 42 days of birth. Satellite table of mfr_nyfoedte.

mfr_barn_kontakter.name: Barn_Kontakter - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_barn_kontakter.description: One row per LPR contact for the child, starting within 42 days of birth. Satellite table of mfr_nyfoedte, structurally the same idea as lpr_a_kontakt but scoped to birth-related contacts only.
mfr_barn_kontakter.joins: DW_EK_Nyfoedt to MFR_NYFOEDTE (many-to-one); DW_EK_Forloeb to MFR_BARN_FORLOEB (many-to-one)

mfr_barn_procedurer.name: Barn_Procedurer - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_barn_procedurer.description: One row per procedure, indication, or procedure add-on code for the child, tied to a contact or course element within 42 days of birth. Structurally the same idea as lpr_a_procregistrering. `Kejsersnit` (on mfr_nyfoedte) is derived from KMCA* rows in this exact table.
mfr_barn_procedurer.joins: DW_EK_Nyfoedt to MFR_NYFOEDTE (many-to-one); DW_EK_Kontakt to MFR_BARN_KONTAKTER (many-to-one); DW_EK_Forloeb to MFR_BARN_FORLOEB (many-to-one)

mfr_barn_resultater.name: Barn_Resultater - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_barn_resultater.description: One row per reported clinical result for the child, tied to a contact or course element within 42 days of birth. `ResultatVaerdi` is polymorphic: the actual data type it holds depends on `ResultatType` (see reader_note).
mfr_barn_resultater.joins: DW_EK_Nyfoedt to MFR_NYFOEDTE (many-to-one); DW_EK_Kontakt to MFR_BARN_KONTAKTER (many-to-one); DW_EK_Forloeb to MFR_BARN_FORLOEB (many-to-one)

mfr_mor_diagnoser.name: Mor_Diagnoser - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_mor_diagnoser.description: One row per diagnosis, contact reason, or diagnosis add-on code for the mother, tied to a contact from the start of pregnancy through 42 days after birth. Structurally the same idea as mfr_barn_diagnoser, mirroring lpr_a_diagnose. `tobaksforbrug`'s DUT* codes are add-on rows in this exact table (DiagnoseType = "+").
mfr_mor_diagnoser.joins: DW_EK_Foedsel to MFR_NYFOEDTE (many-to-one); DW_EK_Kontakt to MFR_MOR_KONTAKTER (many-to-one); DW_EK_Forloeb to MFR_MOR_FORLOEB (many-to-one)

mfr_mor_forloeb.name: Mor_Forloeb - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_mor_forloeb.description: One row per LPR course element ("forloebselement") for the mother, linked to a contact starting from the beginning of pregnancy through 42 days after birth. Satellite table of mfr_nyfoedte, mirroring mfr_barn_forloeb.

mfr_mor_kontakter.name: Mor_Kontakter - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_mor_kontakter.description: One row per LPR contact for the mother, from the start of pregnancy through 42 days after birth. Satellite table of mfr_nyfoedte, mirroring mfr_barn_kontakter.
mfr_mor_kontakter.joins: DW_EK_Foedsel to MFR_NYFOEDTE (many-to-one); DW_EK_Forloeb to MFR_MOR_FORLOEB (many-to-one)

mfr_mor_procedurer.name: Mor_Procedurer - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_mor_procedurer.description: One row per procedure, indication, or procedure add-on code for the mother, tied to a contact or course element from the start of pregnancy through 42 days after birth. Structurally the same idea as mfr_barn_procedurer, mirroring lpr_a_procregistrering.
mfr_mor_procedurer.joins: DW_EK_Foedsel to MFR_NYFOEDTE (many-to-one); DW_EK_Kontakt to MFR_MOR_KONTAKTER (many-to-one); DW_EK_Forloeb to MFR_MOR_FORLOEB (many-to-one)

mfr_mor_resultater.name: Mor_Resultater - MFR 2019+ satellite table
mfr_mor_resultater.description: One row per reported clinical result for the mother, tied to a contact or course element from the start of pregnancy through 42 days after birth. `ResultatVaerdi` is polymorphic, same as mfr_barn_resultater (though this table's documented value shapes omit the boolean/text-string cases seen there).
mfr_mor_resultater.joins: DW_EK_Foedsel to MFR_NYFOEDTE (many-to-one); DW_EK_Kontakt to MFR_MOR_KONTAKTER (many-to-one); DW_EK_Forloeb to MFR_MOR_FORLOEB (many-to-one)

mfr_nyfoedte.name: Nyfoedte - Medicinsk Foedselsregister 2019+
mfr_nyfoedte.description: One row per newborn (live-born or stillborn) in Denmark from 1 January 2019 onwards. Carries basic facts about the child, mother and father plus a curated set of medical facts (birth diagnosis, weight, Apgar score, smoking status, and more) resolved from LPR3 contacts within 42 days of birth (or, for the mother, from the start of pregnancy). Detailed diagnosis/procedure/result history sits in ten satellite tables (family mfr2019) joined via DW_EK_Nyfoedt (child) or DW_EK_Foedsel (mother).
mfr_nyfoedte.joins: CPRnummer_Barn to BEF (many-to-one); DW_EK_Kontakt_Barn to LPR_A_KONTAKT (many-to-one)

mfraccre.name: MFRACCRE - MFR marker sub-cut
mfraccre.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of placenta accreta (abnormal placental attachment) for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_accreta flag.

mfrakmpl.name: MFRAKMPL - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrakmpl.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of other birth complications not covered by the more specific sub-cuts for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_andre_foedselskomplikati flag.

mfranaes.name: MFRANAES - MFR marker sub-cut
mfranaes.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of anaesthesia for an operation for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_anaestesi_til_operation flag.

mfrblodm.name: MFRBLODM - MFR marker sub-cut, postpartum blood loss
mfrblodm.description: One row per postpartum blood-loss finding for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR, with the actual measured amount alongside the SKS code. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_post_partum_bloedning flag. Coverage starts 2009, a decade later than most of the other marker sub-cuts.

mfrbrist.name: MFRBRIST - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrbrist.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of perineal tears for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_perineal_bristning flag.

mfrcardi.name: MFRCARDI - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrcardi.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of cardiomyopathy for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_cardiomyopati flag.

mfrdfoed.name: MFRDFOED - Dødfødsler fra det medicinske fødselsregister
mfrdfoed.description: Supplementary clinical detail for the stillbirth subset of the 1997-2018 Medical Birth Register, joined to mfr.yaml via FK_MFR. Not a standalone population: every row here should also have a row in mfr.yaml with LEVENDE_ELLER_DOEDFOEDT indicating a stillbirth.
mfrdfoed.joins: FK_MFR to MFR (one-to-one); CPR_MODER to BEF (many-to-one)

mfrgkmpl.name: MFRGKMPL - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrgkmpl.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of pregnancy complications for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_graviditetskomplikatio flag.

mfrhaemo.name: MFRHAEMO - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrhaemo.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of haemoperitoneum for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_haemoperitoneum flag.

mfrhjmfo.name: MFRHJMFO - Hjemmefødsler fra det medicinske fødselsregister
mfrhjmfo.description: Supplementary clinical detail for home births within the 1997-2018 Medical Birth Register era, joined to mfr.yaml via FK_MFR. Not a standalone population: every row here also has a row in mfr.yaml, which already flags home births via FOEDESTED/MARKOER_HJEMMEFOEDSEL_BEREGNET.
mfrhjmfo.joins: FK_MFR to MFR (one-to-one); CPR_MODER to BEF (many-to-one)

mfrigang.name: MFRIGANG - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrigang.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of labour induction for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_igangsaettelse flag.

mfrinfek.name: MFRINFEK - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrinfek.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of infections for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_infektioner flag.

mfrkjsnt.name: MFRKJSNT - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrkjsnt.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of caesarean section for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_kejsersnit flag.

mfrmedsg.name: MFRMEDSG - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrmedsg.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of medical conditions for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_medicinske_sygdomme flag.

mfrmisda.name: MFRMISDA - MFR marker sub-cut
mfrmisda.description: One row per SKS-coded finding of congenital malformation for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR. Backs mfr.yaml's markoer_b_misdannelse flag.

mfrnvlan.name: MFRNVLAN - MFR marker sub-cut, umbilical cord blood analysis
mfrnvlan.description: One row per umbilical cord blood analysis result for a birth in mfr.yaml, joined via FK_MFR, with pH and base excess values alongside the SKS code.
